🚀 Good early-career Operations role at Tracelight in London

Tracelight is hiring an Operations Associate to work directly with the Chief of Staff.

📍 London | In-office
💼 Operations | Chief of Staff | Startup | AI
🎓 MBA Relevance: Selective fit for early-career MBAs
📈 Company growth: 10x revenue in 8 months, currently growing ~40% month-on-month
💰 Equity offered

🧭 What you’d actually be doing
This is a very hands-on operator role covering:
• Customer onboarding
• Contracts and invoicing
• Security questionnaires
• Internal tools and processes
• New joiner onboarding
• Office and team operations
• Using AI to make internal workflows more scalable

The company works with Big 4 firms, global advisory businesses and large-cap PE clients, so the exposure could be strong despite the junior title.

🧭 Compass Take
This is best suited to recent graduates and early-career operators who want broad exposure inside a fast-growing startup.
For an MBA with around 3 years of pre-MBA experience, I think it can still make sense, but only if you actively want a startup generalist / operator path and are comfortable with work that includes fairly basic operational tasks.
I would not recommend it to a more experienced MBA expecting a classic post-MBA strategy role, seniority jump, or polished management scope. The title and day-to-day are junior, even if the learning curve could be steep.
They are also asking candidates to show what they’ve built with AI and give concrete examples of ownership, which is a useful signal for how they’re screening.

📩 Apply directly by sending your CV + 3 bullets on why you’re a strong fit to careers@tracelight.ai

Hey #connections 👋
Recently, Ritesh Kumar Gupta, Rohit Akkole, and I participated in a Hackathon organized by Razorpay in collaboration with Replit.

We were asked to use Replit's new AI Harness to build a product, and what we learned was pretty interesting.

Replit felt like a one-stop solution for building and deploying applications, even for people who aren't deeply technical. It takes care of things like storage, security, and deployment, all from one place.

Replit's AI Harness was also really impressive. We were able to build an APP with a single prompt. We first refined the prompt using ChatGPT and then used it in Replit to build the application.

The Harness was able to:
- Create dummy data
- Store it in Replit's database
- Store environment variables securely in the Secret Manager
- Build the application without consuming a huge number of tokens
- Publish the entire application with just one click
We were given $20 worth of tokens, which covered the development and publishing process.

For the hackathon, we built a Headcount Management System - essentially a Workday-like solution focused specifically on headcount, hiring requests, vendor contracts, and workforce forecasting, rather than payroll or benefits.
Managers can:
- Plan their headcount for the year
- Request additional headcount for their teams
- Track planned vs. actual headcount
- Understand hiring requirements and the impact of changes to the plan

HR can review, approve, and dispatch these requests, while everyone gets the same reconciled numbers against actuals every month.

We also added several other features, including an action-taking chatbot with Human-in-the-Loop (HITL).
GitHub: https://lnkd.in/gdTAb5rU

I would have shared the app link as well, but the application was taken down after the hackathon.

Thanks to Razorpay and Replit for hosting this Buildathon. We learned a lot!

- A team dedicated to your projects, not juggling five other clients
- Support that continues after launch, with clear response times

I almost fell for a suspicious job opportunity just because I’m job hunting. 😅

I had just finished applying for a job when I received an email from a “recruiter” almost immediately.

I opened the email with excitement and that little rush of adrenaline you get when you think, “Wait… did someone actually notice me?” 😂

Then I saw the offer:
$70,000–$95,000+ per year for a Lead Executive Virtual Assistant role.

I didn’t apply for this particular role, so I was curious.

The email explained the role, listed responsibilities, and even explained why my background was a good fit.

But then I got to the end of the email and saw this:
“Thanks for sharing your journey. I hope you find the right opportunity soon. If you'd like to discuss career positioning or share ideas about your job search, I'd be glad to connect.”

Wait… what? 😂

That didn’t quite match the rest of the email.

So, instead of getting carried away by the salary, I copied the entire email and sent it to my almighty assistant, Claude AI. 😂

I asked it to explain the email to me like I was 5 years old and help me identify anything suspicious.

And honestly, that was a good decision.

It helped me come up with questions I should ask before sharing my CV:
• Who is the hiring company?
• Who exactly is the recruiter?
• Can I verify the recruiter professionally?
• What is the actual employment/contract structure?
• What are the working hours and time zone?
• What is the exact scope of the role?

I asked.

The recruiter said the company couldn't be disclosed until I was shortlisted and asked me to send my CV.

I then asked for the recruiter's LinkedIn profile.

The response?

“My corporate LinkedIn network portal is currently undergoing an official platform restructuring and security migration…”

Hmm. 😂And here's where it got more interesting: the email addresses kept changing- Gmail, then a company domain, and now another Gmail address.
At that point, I decided not to share my CV until the recruiter and firm could be independently verified.

So basically, every time I asked for something I could use to verify the opportunity, I got a reason why I couldn't verify it.

And that experience reminded me of something important:
Job seekers are vulnerable too.

When you're actively looking for work, an unexpected offer, especially one with an attractive salary, can make you want to move quickly.

But please, don't let excitement make you skip your due diligence.

Before sending your CV or personal information to an unfamiliar recruiter:

-Verify the recruiter
-Check the company
-Ask questions about the role
-Be cautious when information is deliberately vague
-Don't allow an attractive salary to rush your decision
-Never send sensitive personal or financial information to an unverified contact

Sometimes, the best response to a great-looking opportunity isn't “How quickly can I apply?”
It's “Let me verify this first.”

AI Governance: Regulators Now Want Proof, Not Promises

Colorado has an AI law now. New York has one covering AI used in hiring. More states are adding their own every few months. Over 60% of businesses will be required to have a formal AI governance framework this year, according to Gartner. Regulators used to just ask businesses to be careful. Now they’re asking for proof, and most businesses don’t have any.

Here’s how that gap happened. Over the last couple years, businesses rolled out AI fast, chatbots, hiring tools, automated decisions, without writing any of it down. Nobody tracked which tools were in use, what they were actually doing, or who was checking the AI’s decisions before they affected a real person. That was fine when nobody asked. Now someone is asking, and “we’ve just been using it” isn’t going to hold up.

Governance just means having an answer ready. What AI tools are actually running in the business. What each one is used for, and how much risk that use carries. And proof that an actual person reviews anything the AI decides that touches hiring, customers, or sensitive information.

The cost of skipping this isn’t abstract anymore. It’s fines under laws that already exist. And increasingly, it’s clients who won’t sign a contract until you can show them this is handled. In some industries, having this documented isn’t optional anymore, it’s the price of doing business.

This isn’t about using less AI. It’s about being able to show someone, in writing, that a person is actually watching how it gets used.

The Question: Why is international commercial growth expanding at only 26% YoY, while U.S. commercial surges 133% YoY?

Karps Response: Focused on Palantirs belief-driven mission in Europe, remarking: Its not actually in our economic interest anymore to do this, but we still do it... because we are believers.

The Research Reality: While inspiring, it avoids explaining how Palantir plans to reignite lagging European enterprise sales.

2. The Copycat Defense on Margins

The Question: How will Palantir protect its margins against competitors copying its platform?

Karps Response: Joked that we can definitely meet our guide next year if we get paid for all the people copying us, blaming standard software companies for executing outdated playbooks.

The Research Reality: Humor deflects from the real question: How rising technical hiring costs will affect GAAP profit margins through 2026.

'So when executives pivot from cold metrics to philosophy or jokes, researchers highlight it as a area to watch', Divyam jotted down.

INDIAN IT: PREPARING FOR TWO QUARTERS OF SELECTIVE GROWTH

India’s IT industry faces a demanding operating environment. Cautious client spending, longer decision cycles and AI-led pricing pressure are making growth harder to translate into stronger margins.

Large contracts can support order books, but their value depends on execution, billing milestones and timely collections. For smaller IT firms and their delivery partners, payroll and operating expenses continue while customer payments remain outstanding.

Q3 FY 2026–27 | OCTOBER–DECEMBER

Growth could remain restrained as client caution combines with holiday furloughs and fewer billable days. Cost optimisation and vendor consolidation may offer opportunities, although competitive pricing could limit profitability.

Businesses should plan for uneven project starts, tighter utilisation and possible gaps between staff deployment and billing.

Q4 FY 2026–27 | JANUARY–MARCH

Fresh client budgets could support selective improvement if approvals and deal conversions accelerate. AI implementation, cloud modernisation, cybersecurity and efficiency-led projects may offer opportunities.

A broad recovery should not be assumed. Revenue momentum will depend on funded commitments, delivery progress and customers’ willingness to spend.

For promoters and CFOs, the priority is to:

• Align hiring and subcontracting with confirmed project schedules.
• Track unbilled revenue, debtor ageing and customer concentration.
• Stress-test cash flows against delayed starts and collections.
• Maintain liquidity for payroll, cloud costs and delivery commitments.
• Ensure funding repayments match realistic collection cycles.

The future of public sector talent isn’t coming….it’s already been rewritten! 🤔👇🏾

A huge thank you to everyone who came together for the Indeed, Matrix, and PPMA exceptional agenda to discuss and digest the massive shifts reshaping the UK labour market. 😁

The thought provoking sessions and follow on discussions highlighted a critical reality for public sector leaders. We are not just managing headcount, and supporting workforce wellbeing, we are navigating an entirely new psychological and technological contract with the people who have, or we want to have, a public sector career. 💡🤝

Jack Kennedy, Indeed’s Senior Economist,  
 made it clear that in the UK Labour Market Outlook, the economic pressures and shifting worker expectations require a more agile, data-driven approach to recruitment than ever before. 🤔🤝  Tim Stokes, Sales Director, Matrix Security Watchdog, delivered a very sharp truth ‘You can’t manage what you can’t see’. Employees holding multiple roles simultaneously isn't just a trend, it’s a blind spot that public sector governance must address. 🤔🤝

Emma Kearns, Founder, Seren Neurodiversity reminded us that neurodiversity hiring and inclusion isn’t a box-ticking exercise in a deep and profound way. It requires perhaps less structure than we tend to think, and  being much more intentional about workplace design to unlock what is clearly immense, underutilised potential. 🤔🤝

Matt Burney, Senior Advisor on Future of Work, AI & Talent Strategy, Indeed, broke down the four forces of practical AI adoption. AI isn't just a tool to speed up old processes, it is without doubt actively reshaping talent strategy and the very nature of public sector work. 🤔🤝

Trudy Forster’s, Assistant Chief Executive, North Yorkshire Council and PPMA - Public Services People Managers Association Vice President, delivered important insights on Workforce Transformation and Local Government Re-Org that shines a spotlight on the fact that true transformation requires heavy lifting, sustained resilience, and continuous support throughout restructure and beyond. 🤔🤝

The organisations that will attract the best  talent tomorrow will be those that embrace transparency, leverage AI ethically, design for neuroinclusion, and adapt to the fluid reality of future and modern employment. Organisations will achieve continuous growth, just based on their commitments to the community, but clearly there are also some limitations on what can be achieved, particularly when change is required at pace. 
🤔🤝

The take away for me personally was what an enormous amount could be achieved in partnership!! 🤝🤩

As ever, inspired and uplifted, by the fact that we can continue to make a huge difference together! Looking forward to more conversations too! 🤝😁🤩👇🏾

7 Direct Threats to the Indian BPO Industry

The Indian BPO industry is entering a phase where traditional cost and manpower advantages may no longer be enough.

1. AI & Automation replacing traditional BPO processes
Impact: Lower headcount requirements, reduced transaction-based billing, and pressure on traditional outsourcing models.

2. Global economic slowdown & cautious client spending
Impact: Lower revenues, delayed expansion, hiring freezes, pricing pressure, and margin compression.

3. Geopolitical conflicts & global trade disruptions
Impact: Cost escalation, currency volatility, delayed client decisions, and business-continuity risks.

4. Cybersecurity threats & customer data breaches
Impact: Financial penalties, higher compliance costs, reputational damage, and potential client attrition.

5. Competition from GCCs & alternative outsourcing destinations
Impact: Greater competition for deals, pricing pressure, and the need to demonstrate measurable business value beyond labor arbitrage.

6. Rising operating costs & shrinking margins
Impact: Greater productivity pressure, workforce optimization, site consolidation, and difficult cost decisions.

7. Stricter client expectations & evolving quality models
Impact: Higher service-level expectations, contract penalties, increased rework, and potential loss of business.

My perspective on the biggest structural change

The biggest long-term challenge may not be a global recession or geopolitical conflict.

It is the transformation from a manpower-based outsourcing model to a technology-enabled, outcome-based service model.

For BPO leaders, the future will require more than people management. It will require strong capabilities in:

• Operational excellence
• Process redesign
• AI & automation governance
• Quality analytics
• Digital transformation
• Outcome-based delivery

The question is no longer simply: “How efficiently can we manage people?”

It is increasingly becoming:

“How effectively can we combine people, technology and intelligence to deliver measurable business outcomes?”

That shift could define the next phase of the Indian BPO industry.
